doc.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: Monk Rowe's introduction; the Benny Goodman Story and a school metal clarinet
summary: Rowe introduces Militello. In fourth grade he saw the Benny Goodman Story, asked for clarinet lessons, and the school lent him a metal Buescher clarinet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and we are in Buffalo, New York filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. I’m very pleased to have Bobby Militello with me today. I’ve been looking forward to talking to you because you see the music business from at least two sides.
Whatever possessed you to become a player first?

Well I’ve always had the talent or the thing about playing, but when I was in fourth grade my mother took me to see the “Benny Goodman Story” and the next day, the next day I went to school and asked could I take clarinet lessons. And we were pretty poor and so the school gave me a clarinet and it started with that.
Wow. Was it a metal one?
Yeah, oh yeah, it was a metal clarinet and it was actually an old Buescher, which I wish I still had, even though it was the metal one I still wouldn’t mind having that.
Yeah well they make good lamps too.
Yeah I know. I hate that. When I go into somebody’s house and there’s a violin on the wall or a saxophone with a light coming out of the bell it’s like oh.
